title: SDK modularization and test matrix
author: Aisha Mehta
body:
Summary

This doc defines patterns for componentizing Redwood client SDKs, the canonical compatibility/test matrix we gate on CI, and a prescriptive migration checklist for teams breaking large SDK monoliths into smaller adapter-capability packages. It also lists the top related support patterns we expect after modularization and the canonical fixes/escapes to reduce customer-facing incidents.

Context and goals

Why modularize? SDK modularization reduces release blast radius, enables language-idiomatic adapters, allows smaller client footprints for embedded runtimes, and makes per-feature rollouts (streaming, embeddings, token-cost telemetry) safer. Goals:
- Reduce SDK surface area changes from large releases.
- Provide a single compatibility matrix for runtime modes (hosted/dedicated/private).
- Ensure automated CI test coverage across languages and common integration patterns.
- Provide a migration checklist that minimizes downstream breakages for customers.

When to apply

Use this guide when:
1) An SDK exceeds ~50k LOC or bundles >5 optional features into a single package.
2) Teams need to ship language-specific adapters (Node, Python, Go, Java) with different runtime constraints (browser vs server vs edge).
3) You need to enable per-feature rollouts (e.g., streaming-only upgrade) or to remove a deprecated transport.

Recommended component boundaries (opinionated)

- core-client: network, authentication, stable request/response types, retries, and telemetry hooks. Minimal dependency set.
- io-adapters: transport implementations (fetch, axios, requests, grpc). They implement a small transport interface and are optional packages.
- streaming: streaming helpers and backpressure primitives (server-sent events, web-socket reconnection policies).
- tooling: CLI tooling for local replay, recording, and snippet generation (separate package).
- feature-adapters: embeddings, reranking, structured-output (each as optional sub-packages).
- dev-utils: local emulation harnesses and test fixtures (dev-only dependency).

Design rules (must-haves)

1) core-client must not depend directly on io-adapters; use an interface injected at runtime.
2) Every public package must maintain a compatibility matrix file (COMPAT.md) listing minimum runtime and server API expectations.
3) Semantic versioning for each package; coordinated multi-package releases are allowed only with a documented release note and migration guide.
4) Backwards-compatible proto for request/response shapes for at least two minor versions.

Compatibility and test matrix (canonical gate)

We run the following matrix in CI for every merge to main. A passing run means the package is eligible for publish. Failing runs block release.

ASCII table:

| Package | Language / Platform | Runtime Modes | Minimum Server API | Smoke tests | Integration tests | E2E sample | Owner |
|---------|---------------------|---------------|--------------------|-------------|-------------------|-----------|-------|
| core-client | python | server, private | v2025-10 | unit, linters | auth + retry | samples/py/basic | sdk-py |
| io-adapter-fetch | node | browser, edge | v2025-10 | unit | transport-handshake | samples/js/browser-repl | sdk-js |
| streaming | node, python | server, browser | v2025-11 | unit | chunked-response | samples/js/streaming | sdk-stream |
| embeddings-adapter | python | server | v2025-09 | unit | embedding-dedup + accuracy smoke | samples/py/embeddings | sdk-emb |
| cli-tooling | go | developer | n/a | unit | fs-perf + snapshot | samples/go/cli | sdk-cli |

Minimum tests for each package (detailed):
- Unit: 100% critical path functions covered, mock transports for network layer.
- Lint & static analysis: type checks (mypy/tsc/Go vet).
- Smoke: authenticate, simple generate/embedding, graceful error handling.
- Integration: run against staging Redwood runtime (dedicated staging) for at least the following: auth token rotation, retry on 5xx, rate-limit header handling.
- E2E sample: run sample app in ephemeral infra (local emulation or ephemeral cluster) and assert end-to-end observable metrics (latency < configured SLO for sample).

CI gating details

- Each package has its own CI pipeline file at .github/workflows/<package>.yml.
- Matrix runs in parallel per-language. Fail-fast is enabled for unit + lint stages.
- Integration tests acquire a short-lived staging API key via the secrets manager; the key is restricted to the staging cluster.
- Releases are automated with a 'release-candidate' tag; final publish requires a manual approval step for cross-package coordinated changes.

Migration checklist (ordered, minimal friction)

1) Identify boundary: list functions/types being moved with rationale.
2) Create target package skeleton with README and COMPAT.md.
3) Add adapter interface in core-client (if not present) and add adapter injection tests.
4) Port tests to the new package and keep a shim in core-client that forwards calls (deprecation shim).
5) Add CI pipeline for new package and run full matrix.
6) Publish a pre-release (rc) and update sample applications to depend on rc.
7) Monitor staging integrations for 72 hours, collect telemetry for errors and latency regressions.
8) Announce deprecation timeline in release notes with code migration examples.

Deprecation shim pattern (example)

- core-client should export a thin shim that imports and re-exports the adapter API with a deprecation notice in runtime logs. Example (pseudo-js):

```js
// core-client/src/adapters.js
export function defaultTransport(opts) {
  console.warn('[DEPRECATION] defaultTransport is moved to @redwood/io-fetch. See migration guide.');
  return require('@redwood/io-fetch').default(opts);
}
```

Top support issues to anticipate and canonical fixes

1) Install/packaging mismatches (node bundlers):
- Symptom: customers using modern bundlers (esbuild/webpack/rollup) see 'fs not found' or large bundle sizes.
- Cause: server-only modules included in browser builds.
- Canonical fix: provide an explicit browser entry in package.json, publish ESM + CJS builds, and split io-adapter packages so browser bundle excludes server transports.
- Quick triage steps: check package.json "browser" field, reproduce with esbuild --bundle --platform=browser.

2) Transport mismatch (timeouts and retries double-applied):
- Symptom: duplicate retry delays; requests last longer than expected.
- Cause: both adapter and consumer apply retries.
- Canonical fix: introduce and document a single retry policy owner (core-client) and add a disableRetries flag for adapters.
- Patch: release minor with default disableRetries: true on adapter constructors.

3) Version skew between core-client and feature-adapters causing missing types at runtime:
- Symptom: runtime TypeError for missing field in request payload.
- Cause: adapters published against a newer core request contract.
- Canonical fix: enforce compatibility using the COMPAT.md and add runtime assertion on import that checks core-client version and warns early with actionable migration link.

4) Streaming partials not delivered (chunk merging issues):
- Symptom: consumer receives partial tokens out of order or truncated.
- Cause: adapters using different chunk framing conventions.
- Canonical fix: standardize a framing header and provide a small reference helper in streaming package. Add a dedicated integration test that replays chunked frames with network jitter.

Example COMPAT.md snippet (recommended)

"""
Package: @redwood/core-client
Compatible with: server API v2025-09 through v2026-02
Minimum Node: 14.20 (LTS)
Minimum Python: 3.9
Transport contract: expects adapter to implement `send(request: Request): Promise<Response>` and to honor `disableRetries` boolean on options.
"""

Release notes and communication guidance

- Each package release must include: what's changed, migration steps (copy-paste ready), and a compatibility table.
- For breaking changes, publish a short migration guide and open a docs PR with before/after snippets.
- Notify customer-success for any change that touches core-client or streaming packages; coordinate a one-week monitoring window post-release.

Operational runbook (quick)

1) If downstream samples fail after a package split:
  a) Check the CI matrix for the sample app pipeline and find failing stage.
  b) Check the published package versions used by the sample.
  c) Reproduce locally using the exact published versions: pip/pnpm install <version>.
  d) If failure is due to version skew, roll dependency to matching RC and open a fix PR.

2) If a customer reports bundle breakage in browser:
  a) Ask for bundler and config; reproduce with minimal reproducible repo.
  b) Confirm that package.json has "exports"/"browser" fields and provide temporary workaround (use dynamic import of server-only paths).

Appendix: small test matrix YAML example (CI job snippet)

```yaml
name: package-matrix
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  test-matrix:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    strategy:
      matrix:
        package: [core-client, io-adapter-fetch, streaming]
        lang: [node, python]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Setup ${{ matrix.lang }}
        run: |
          if [ "${{ matrix.lang }}" = "node" ]; then nvm install 18; fi
          if [ "${{ matrix.lang }}" = "python" ]; then python -m venv .venv; fi
      - run: ./scripts/ci-run.sh ${{ matrix.package }} ${{ matrix.lang }}
```
